📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-04-crm-amqp-consumer-monitor-family-quiet-period-flap`
This is occurrence #11 in the last 7 days (123 total since 2026-07-04; degraded-mode cycle, no live Slack alert to confirm against).
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `CRM Experience` (runtime-core-subscriber-api) / `Admin` (mobile-notifications-stack) — split by service, DD tag says `team:crm` for both
Playbook: Confirm shape via dd_search.py metric sum:trace.amqp.command.hits{service:<name>,env:prod}.as_rate() over a multi-hour window — expect a genuine but brief dip below the monitor's floor, not a data gap/tool failure; confirm 0 error logs for the window; check sibling monitors in the family before escalating.

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-05-21-gateway-microservices-timeout`
This is occurrence #21 in the last 7 days (670 total since 2026-05-20).
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Admin` (`@admin` / `#team-admin`)
Playbook: 1) Confirm chronic baseline by comparing ES Ocelot.Responder.Middleware Warning volume in the alert window vs the same window 24h ago — if delta < 20%, it's the chronic pattern (no new incident). 2) Aggregate timeouts by RequestPath: if dominant paths are all under upstream microservices.methodlocal.int, it's pool-level. 3) Check ki-dns-microservices-method-int-pps-quota first — DNS bursts on the Windows fleet present here as Ocelot timeouts. 4) If DNS is clean: identify which downstream microservice owns the slow path via Ocelot config in ms-gateway-api/gateway/API/ocelot.*.json. 5) Decision tree for the fix: (a) raise per-route Ocelot timeout, (b) scale microservices IIS pool / shorten recycle interval, (c) profile the upstream microservice under prod load.
Open Jira: n/a
